observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a silver-tone pendant necklace resting on a white/cream padded fabric surface. The pendant has a central round-to-oval iridescent (aurora/moonstone-like) gemstone set in a starburst/snowflake halo of clear baguette and round-cut crystals, hanging from a bail studded with small stones. A portion of the chain and an open lobster clasp are visible above and to the right of the pendant.
visible_changes: The central iridescent stone continuously shifts its play of color across the frames—flashes of blue, teal, green, pink, orange and white appear in different regions of the stone as the viewing angle changes, indicating the pendant (or camera) is tilting/rotating relative to the light.

The pendant, bail, chain and lobster clasp translate and reorient slightly within the frame (e.g., the clasp moves from lower-center-left toward upper-right and back), so the whole jewelry piece drifts across the view rather than staying fixed.
The background fabric and its right-side seam/edge also shift position relative to the frame edges, consistent with a change in viewpoint or a moved display.
The starburst halo's spike orientation tilts a few degrees between frames, matching the pendant's slight rotation.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pendant is being held/rotated by an unseen hand or the camera itself is panning—no operator or support is visible.
The state of the necklace before and after this excerpt (it is not shown being clasped, worn, or placed).
The exact gemstone material and metal type.
uncertain_details: Distinguishing object motion from camera motion is not possible from the frames alone, since both the pendant and the fabric background shift together.
The pendant's overall shape and size remain constant (no deformation); observed changes are orientation/position and color reflection, not physical alteration.
